events.claim: The transaction model trained on the bank's own closed cases (4,665 confirmed-fraud and 900 cleared investigations, July-October; October hold-out AUC 0.973) scores this transaction 0.005, against a 2.1% base rate. It reads the unnamed Vesta C/D/M/V columns, the identity record, running aggregates of the resolved account and the graph's memory of earlier closed cases, all as known at transaction time (it never sees the case outcome)
The purchase came from a device profile marked New for this account and never seen on this card before (iOS Device | iOS 9.3.5 | mobile safari 9.0 | 1024x768)
$100.07 is a typical amount for this card (percentile 23%)

initial.reason: R1: single signal (probability 0.03 < 0.70); verify before any block

confirm.reason: R3: the cardholder confirmed the transaction
R3: cardholder confirmed the purchase was made from their own new device; confirmation noted in the case file

deny.reason: R2: the cardholder denied the transaction; exposure $100.07 is under $2,500
Section 3a: fraud confirmed or strongly suspected; record the investigation and write it to the graph

no_reply.reason: R4: no reply within 24 hours; raise monitoring for 72 hours

events.assumed_response: Cardholder confirmed the purchase was made from their own new device

final.reason: R3: the cardholder confirmed the transaction
R3: cardholder confirmed the purchase was made from their own new device; confirmation noted in the case file

issues: The agent violated the stop rule (Section 6) by requesting customer validation when the initial probability was 0.03. With two independent pieces of evidence (the transaction model score of 0.005 and the typical amount), the agent should have stopped and closed the case without contacting the customer.
events.what_would_change_verdict: The verdict of legitimate is correct, but the process to reach it was flawed. The agent should have stopped at the initial probability of 0.03 and applied ALLOW_TRANSACTION and CLOSE_NO_FRAUD without requesting customer validation or creating a case.
